baseline: Each flock sign is compared with the flock's own previous 7 days, leaving out days with a meter or supply fault.
birds_note: Water per bird uses the live-hen count from the DailyLog (last mortality entry 2026-09-13); after that the last known count is carried forward.

signs.label: Daily water per bird
signs.message: 409 ml/bird/day — within the last week's normal (338–568).
signs.research: A sudden change in daily water, especially a drop, is often the earliest sign of a health or supply problem.

signs.label: Drinking start after lights-on
signs.message: Started 07:50, 130 min after lights-on — within the last week's normal (11–189).
signs.research: A late or sluggish morning start can mean a flock that is unwell or water that is not reaching the drinkers.

signs.label: Drinking around dusk
signs.message: 28% — within the last week's normal (25%–49%).
signs.research: Laying hens normally drink heavily in the hours before dark; losing that evening peak is a behaviour change.

signs.label: A-frame 1 share of water
signs.message: 50% — within the last week's normal (42%–58%).
signs.research: The two A-frames hold similar flocks, so a shift in balance points to a local line, drinker or meter problem.

signs.label: Flock activity (noise)
signs.message: 3.1 dB above night — within the last week's normal (1.7–5.7).
signs.research: Changes in flock sound level accompany stress and illness; a quieter day can mean lethargic birds.

signs.label: Water used at night (22:00–05:00)
signs.message: A-frame 1 0 L, A-frame 2 0 L overnight — close to zero, as expected in the dark.
signs.research: Hens stop drinking after lights-out; flow in the dark points to leaks, flushing, light leaks or disturbed birds.

signs.label: One A-frame dry while the other drinks
signs.message: A-frame 1 (WM1) read 0 L from 07:00 to 08:00 while A-frame 2 drank 30 L — a single hour, often just a slow start on one frame.
signs.research: Uneven or interrupted flow points to blocked lines, closed valves or meter faults rather than the birds.

signs.label: Heat load (THI above comfort)
signs.message: 0 h above the 27.8 °C-eq comfort threshold (peak THI 26.3, house max 29.7 °C).
signs.research: Water-to-feed ratio climbs from about 2:1 at 21 °C to 8:1 at 38 °C; heat raises water need and stresses birds.

notes: Snapshot built from raw meter (10-minute) and climate readings; water from the cumulative pulse counters at 10 L per pulse.
Per-A-frame bird numbers are unknown, so water is judged for the whole house per live bird; per-frame readings are used only for balance and dry-frame checks.
Lights-on and lights-off are measured from the climate sensors' light index, not taken from a schedule.
Flock noise is broadband and includes fan noise; activity is daytime noise above the night fan-on level.
Thresholds (2 and 3.5 robust spreads for watch and alert; night water ≥ 30 L; a frame dry ≥ 2 h) are demo defaults, not approved alert rules.
